title: Revenue Forecast & Variance Review
question: How does a transparent forecast compare with reported sales?
method: Annual rolling-origin baseline: project next fiscal year revenue at 5% above the preceding year, then compare with FY2024 and FY2025 actuals. The 5% rate is an illustrative fixed budget assumption, not company guidance or a pre-registered forecast. FY2026 scenarios separately apply product growth of 0/3/6% and service growth of 5/10/15%.
result: FY2025 reported revenue exceeded the illustrative budget by $5.57bn. FY2026 base-case revenue is $436.29bn.
limits: Two annual comparisons are a worked FP&A example, not a statistically validated forecasting model. Annual public reports do not reveal internal monthly budgets, unit volumes or price changes. Scenario assumptions are analyst-created.

title: Integrated Three-Statement Model
question: Do operating assumptions flow consistently into cash and the balance sheet?
method: FY2025 audited closing balance sheet is the opening position. FY2026 scenario: products +3%, services +10%, COGS proportional to revenue, opex +5%, D&A/capex/AR/inventory/AP proportional to revenue. Hold other balance-sheet lines constant, other expense at $321m and dividends at $15,421m. Apply FY2025 effective tax rate. No buybacks, new debt, SBC or OCI in this simplified scenario. D&A is included in operating costs and added back only in CFO.
result: Projected closing cash is $137.98bn. The balance sheet balances to numerical precision, with retained earnings linked to net income and dividends.
limits: This is an analyst scenario, not Apple guidance. Omitting buybacks and other financing means it cannot be interpreted as a likely cash balance. Public filing aggregates constrain operating detail.
